nodes.label: Console Decisions Log
nodes.rationale: The tie-breaker over the self-contradicting design bundle: where a design document and this file disagree, this file wins, and a reopened question needs a new row rather than a component change. Precedence: the CHANGELOG's newest entry usually governs; the prototype (turn 4a for team mode, 6a/7a otherwise) governs where prose is silent; a measured argument beats an aesthetic one; standing rule 1 always holds. 19 rulings recorded.

nodes.label: Design Bundle (agents-team-ui-docs)
nodes.rationale: agents-team-ui-docs/design/: README.md, CHANGELOG.md, MESSAGING.md, and the Octo Session Console prototype (dc.html). Lives in an unversioned sibling repository because the design folder is a re-pulled mirror of a Claude Design project - versioning it here would record someone else's edit history. It contradicts itself in about twenty places; read the newest-first CHANGELOG first when implementing against it.

nodes.label: Standing Rule 1: No Control Without a Runtime Call
nodes.rationale: A control that names no runtime call does not ship. It removes controls with no backing call; a control whose call exists is rule 1 obeyed, not evaded (ruling 12 kept respawn because POST /api/agents/{name}/respawn is a real lead-inbox write).

nodes.label: Standing Rule 3: No Field Without a Source
nodes.rationale: A field with no data source is blank for every operator, and nobody reports a blank. Grounds for ruling 17: the PR field was refused because a local read-only console makes no forge API calls and .git/config yields the repo, never the pull request; diffstat scoped to uncommitted work because branch-against-base means guessing main.

nodes.label: Standing Rule 4: Prototype Contradiction vs Predating Prose
nodes.rationale: Do not write what the prototype does not do - but the rule guards against prose the reference build contradicts, not prose it predates. Ruling 15 kept the read-only markings the prototype never drew: it was drawn before the single-composer model existed, so its silence is an absence, not a disagreement, and the newest voice governs.

nodes.label: Quiet Metadata Register
nodes.rationale: Small quiet metadata text (column headers, footers, meta/hint lines, key legends, empty states, timestamps, receipts, read-only markings, the composer glyph) is --color-neutral-600 with a 10px floor, not target - measured contrast on --color-bg: neutral-700 is 2.69:1, neutral-600 is 4.09:1; contrast beats taste. Text already at 10.5/11px stays; match neighbours in the same pane. Does NOT cover neutral-700 used as a status/state colour or as border/shadow/gutter tokens - recolouring those would be standing rule 2's mistake in the other direction.

nodes.label: Context Warning Threshold Formula
nodes.rationale: Ruling 2: the ! warning fires on the displayed percent, tokens/contextLimit >= 0.75, because a configurable '75%' that lights at 63% on screen is a setting the operator cannot verify. The note fires halfway from the threshold to compactAt and reports distance to compactAt in tokens. No model in catalog.json inverts the two stages (compactAt is 83.5% of 200k, 96.7% of 1M).

nodes.label: Unified Chat Bubble Grounds
nodes.rationale: Ruling 7a: one colour pair for both rooms - left speaker neutral-900 fill / neutral-800 edge / neutral-200 text, right speaker accent-700 fill / accent-600 edge. accent-900 with inset accent-500 is the selected-row tint everywhere else, so a bubble on it reads as a selection; the chosen pair measures 5.6:1. One constant consumed by both rooms so they cannot drift, same reasoning as max-width: 64%.

nodes.label: Respawn Card Kept
nodes.rationale: Ruling 12: the failure card's respawn control ships because it is backed by POST /api/agents/{name}/respawn - a lead-inbox write (src/server/http.ts:374). The card names what the call does (asks the lead to respawn the teammate) and must never imply the console restarts a process.

nodes.label: PR Field Refused, Diffstat Shipped
nodes.rationale: Ruling 17: the picker row carries +N/-M for what is uncommitted against HEAD; nothing names a PR. gh is optional, a forge API needs a token and per-forge client which a local read-only console has none of, and refs/remotes/*/pull/* exists only if hand-fetched.

nodes.label: Read-Only Column Marking
nodes.rationale: Ruling 15: every non-lead wall column and the rail's non-lead pane carry a read-only marking, though the prototype draws none. Without it, a column with no composer is indistinguishable from one whose composer failed to render. Ruled by the team lead during the one-composer close-out.

nodes.label: Workflow Bar Shed Order
nodes.rationale: Ruling 18: totals, then elapsed, then taskId - lower survives longer, mirroring the team bar's precedent that identity outlives figures. The task id is the one metric not re-derivable from the view below; totals go first because the agents view carries them in full. The shed mechanism moved into the shared Bar so both modes shed, each with its own order. Measured: with all three shed the bar's remaining furniture still costs 741.48px.

nodes.label: Run-Picker Trigger Width Bound
nodes.rationale: Ruling 19: min(236px, 26vw) with the name ellipsised and the runId and caret never shrunk. Two terms because one number cannot serve both ends: 236px is what the 1180px design width can spare; 26vw covers the narrow end where 741.48px of un-sheddable furniture leaves at most 27.79% of a 700px frame. A max-width and never flex-shrink - every bar child is flex: none, and a shrinkable one would wrap and double the bar's height. A half-drawn runId identifies nothing.
